data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Phyllis was a Maenad, a follower of Dionysus. She was a beautiful wood nymph who fell in love with the god, but he abandoned her. In her grief, she prayed to the gods to be transformed into a tree, and they answered her prayer. The goddess Cybele turned her into a sycamore tree, and Zeus sent a horned stag to keep her company. Phyllis' name comes from the Greek word phyllon, meaning 'leaf'.
